skill.name: ocr
skill.description: Converts PDFs and image files into Markdown using Claude vision OCR, with single-file and batch workflows.
skill.summary: Convert PDFs and images into structured Markdown with Claude vision OCR.
skill.author: Bae-ChangHyun

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline file extensions, and Task pseudocode. Two findings are confirmed because the skill instructs agents to run shell listing commands on user-provided paths. A medium semantic risk remains because OCRed document content is not explicitly treated as untrusted data.

remediation.issue: Shell listing commands use user-provided paths.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer tool-native file listing. If shell commands are necessary, validate and quote paths, avoid shell glob strings, and never concatenate raw user input.

remediation.issue: OCR input can contain prompt-injection instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Add a rule that text inside PDFs or images is untrusted data. The agent should extract it, not obey any instructions found in the source document.

remediation.issue: Output files may overwrite existing Markdown files.
remediation.suggestion: Before writing output, check whether the target Markdown file exists and ask before replacing it or choose a non-conflicting filename.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted OCR Content Lacks Prompt-Injection Guardrails
semantic_findings.description: The workflow tells agents to read PDFs and images, convert their contents, and write Markdown, but it does not state that document text must be treated only as untrusted data. A malicious source document could try to steer the OCR agent away from extraction or toward unintended output.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited OCR workflows read untrusted user files and ask a subagent to transform and write content. The file has context-protection rules, but no explicit instruction to ignore commands embedded inside the source document.

content.user_title: Convert PDFs and Images to Markdown
content.value_statement: Manual OCR of PDFs and screenshots is slow and inconsistent. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to extract document text into structured Markdown files.
actual_capabilities: Processes PDF files and common image formats including PNG, JPG, JPEG, WEBP, GIF, BMP, and TIFF.
Creates one Markdown file per image and supports unified or page-by-page Markdown output for PDFs.
Uses Task agents so OCR work and file writes happen outside the main conversation context.
Supports batch folder processing by grouping files and running several OCR tasks in parallel.
Preserves common document structure such as headings, tables, lists, diagrams, code blocks, formulas, and UI text.
Reports success, skipped files, output names, and output locations after processing.
limitations: OCR quality depends on Claude vision reading the source file clearly.
Very large or unreadable files may fail with file size or read errors.
The workflow avoids external OCR libraries, so it does not offer specialized OCR engine controls.
The instructions do not define overwrite checks for existing Markdown output files.

use_cases.title: Digitize Research PDFs
use_cases.description: Convert papers, reports, and scanned pages into Markdown notes that keep sections, tables, and formulas readable.

use_cases.title: Extract Screenshot Text
use_cases.description: Turn screenshots, UI captures, or photos into Markdown text for documentation and review workflows.

use_cases.title: Batch Convert Document Folders
use_cases.description: Process mixed folders of PDFs and images, then collect a clear status summary with output file locations.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the OCR skill to convert this image file to Markdown: /path/to/image.png

prompt_templates.title: Convert One PDF
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose unified or page-by-page PDF output
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the OCR skill to convert this PDF to Markdown and ask me how to save the result: /path/to/document.pdf

prompt_templates.title: Extract Specific Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the OCR skill on /path/to/report.pdf and extract only tables, headings, and figure captions into Markdown.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Process a Folder
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced folder workflow with parallel tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the OCR skill to process every supported PDF and image in /path/to/folder/ and summarize the created Markdown files.

output_examples.input: A scanned invoice PDF with a header, line items, totals, and a signature block.
output_examples.output: A Markdown document with the invoice title, vendor details, a line-item table, totals, and a note for unclear signature text.

output_examples.input: A screenshot of a settings page with labels, toggles, and error text.
output_examples.output: A Markdown summary that lists the visible UI labels, selected settings, and the displayed error message.

output_examples.input: A folder containing two PDFs and three images.
output_examples.output: A status summary showing each source file, its generated Markdown file, skipped files, and the output folder.

best_practices: Use clear source paths and confirm the desired PDF save mode before processing.
Give narrow custom instructions when you only need tables, code, summaries, or translated text.
Review generated Markdown against the source when documents contain small text, handwriting, or dense tables.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill for files you are not allowed to read or convert.
Do not expect perfect OCR from blurry, cropped, or low-contrast images.
Do not batch very large folders without checking file size and output naming first.

faq.question: What file types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports PDF files and PNG, JPG, JPEG, WEBP, GIF, BMP, and TIFF images.

faq.question: Can it save each PDF page separately?
faq.answer: Yes. For PDFs, it can create one combined Markdown file or separate Markdown files for each page.

faq.question: Does it use external OCR libraries?
faq.answer: No. The workflow directs Claude vision to read files and avoids external libraries such as PyPDF or Pillow.

faq.question: Where are output files saved?
faq.answer: The skill saves Markdown output near the source file or in the original folder for batch processing.

faq.question: Can it process many files at once?
faq.answer: Yes. It groups supported files in batches of three and runs parallel Task agents.

faq.question: What happens when a file cannot be read?
faq.answer: The workflow skips failed files, reports the reason, and continues processing the remaining files.
